page: Microsoft Azure M128 is a memory-optimized server from the MS family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 128 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 64 physical cores running at 2.7 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 2048.0 GB of RAM, providing 16.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 14680 GB of local storage. No GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 10%, alongside single-threaded compression tasks. Conversely, multi-core execution is strong, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is a key strength, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 426.47 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% tier. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput also demonstrate strong top-25% performance.

The M128 offers high resource density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that can leverage its massive memory footprint and high multi-core parallelism, despite its lower single-core efficiency. It is well-suited for large-scale databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, and multi-threaded data processing. However, it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or real-time text generation in large language models, where text generation speeds for small and medium models rank in the bottom 10%.
description: The Microsoft Azure M128 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores. Operating at 2.7 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 2048.0 GB of RAM (16.0 GB per core) and 14680 GB of local storage, without GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff: single-core metrics and single-threaded compression rank in the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth are highly competitive. Specifically, large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaches a top-tier 426.47 GB/sec, and multi-core CPU tests place in the top 25%. This profile makes the M128 qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-dense, highly parallelized workloads. It is best suited for large-scale databases, multi-threaded data processing, and memory-intensive enterprise applications, rather than single-threaded operations or real-time LLM text generation.
